We identify broad conditions under which, nevertheless, sequential equilibria are guaranteed to achieve a constant fraction of the first-best gains from trade. Our bounds quantify the central role of rare pessimistic seller signals and rare optimistic buyer signals. The results apply to seller-proposer, buyer-proposer, and random-proposer mechanisms. The key idea in our analysis is to relate equilibrium gains from trade to proposer profits in an auxiliary market with independent private values.
item.dc:creator: Naveen Durvasula, Tim Roughgarden

item.title: Almost Optimal Lower Bounds under Almost ETH for Approximating Euclidean k-means
item.description: arXiv:2611.14892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the Euclidean $k$-means problem, we are given a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and the goal is to find $k$ representative points in space so as to minimize the sum of the squared distances from each point to its closest representative. Algorithmically, de la Vega, Karpinski, Kenyon, and Rabani [STOC'03] and Kumar, Sabharwal, and Sen [JACM'10] obtain a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for high-dimensional Euclidean $k$-means in time $2^{(k/\varepsilon)^{O(1)}} \cdot dn^{O(1)}$, which was subsequently improved to $2^{\tilde{O}(k/\varepsilon)} + O(ndk)$ by Feldman, Monemizadeh, and Sohler [SoCG'07]. On the lower-bound side, a recent work of Cohen-Addad, Karthik, Saulpic, and Schwiegelshohn [SoCG'26] proposed the Exponential Time for Expanders Hypothesis (XXH), which asserts exponential-time hardness for $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximating Vertex Cover on vertex expanders, and used it to prove nearly matching running time lower bound whenever $k=\tilde{\omega}(1/\varepsilon)$. We observe that XXH does not hold in the parameter regime needed for the above result, and show how to repair their reduction under a more standard assumption. More precisely, we show that assuming the Almost Exponential Time Hypothesis for 3-SAT (Almost ETH), for every constant $\beta\in(0,1)$, Euclidean $k$-means in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has no $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm running in time $2^{(k/\varepsilon)^{1-\beta}}\text{poly}(n,d)$, whenever $k=\tilde{\omega}(1/\varepsilon)$. By modifying the construction, we also obtain a similar result for approximating the Euclidean $k$-median problem.
item.dc:creator: Karthik C. S., Dor Minzer

item.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.15201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study sparse matrix multiplication in the low-bandwidth model: $n$ computers multiply two $n\times n$ matrices, and each computer can send and receive one $O(\log n)$-bit message per round. The input matrices are uniformly sparse, meaning that there are at most $d$ nonzero entries in each row and column, and the task is to compute a uniformly sparse part of their product. In prior work, Gupta et al.~(SPAA 2022) presented an $O(d^{1.907})$-round algorithm over fields for this problem when the sparsity structure is globally known in advance (this is referred to as the supported setting). The upper bound was later improved to $O(d^{1.832})$ rounds. In this work, we give a deterministic algorithm that solves this problem in $O(d^{3/2})$ rounds in the supported setting, improving the previous bounds over fields and semirings.
item.dc:creator: Chetan Gupta, Jukka Suomela, Hossein Vahidi

item.title: Optimal-Time Independent Subset Sampling over Acyclic Joins
item.description: arXiv:2611.15675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Join results can greatly exceed their inputs even when applications need only a small random subset. We study sampling that includes each result independently with a prescribed probability given by the product of its input-tuple weights (PRODUCT). For fixed full acyclic joins with static weights, we achieve input-linear preprocessing and index space together with output-linear expected sampling work, eliminating logarithmic factors from previous bounds. A shared join-tree index supports weighted draws over the entire join and locates high-probability results. Direct Bernoulli trials handle high-probability results, allowing Poisson thinning to generate the remaining independent inclusion decisions with bounded overhead. Our exact sampler uses expected $O(N)$ preprocessing, $O(N)$ index space, and expected $O(1+m\mu)$ time per call including output construction. Here $N$ is the input size, $m$ counts relation occurrences, and $\mu$ is the expected sample size. The guarantees hold on a real random-access machine with unit-cost exact arithmetic and logarithms, continuous uniform randomness, and expected-time hashing. The time bounds are optimal, matching input reading and explicit output writing. Our floating-point prototype has lower sampling latency than the fastest applicable baseline in 17 of 18 PRODUCT settings on three queries over the STATS benchmark. Construction savings on large joins can offset indexed materialization's faster sampling over a limited number of calls. On a real-data path at $\mu=100$, our sampler achieves a $20.5\times$ speedup over indexed materialization for construction plus 300 calls, measured after common data preparation and loading.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Liu, Zijian Zhang, Zhen Li

item.title: Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
item.description: arXiv:2611.15748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach. While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Blankenburg, Antonia Ellerbrock, Thomas Kesselheim, Jens Vygen

item.title: Efficient Influence Minimization via Source-Integrated Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.15949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Influence minimization by node blocking is a fundamental problem in graph data management that seeks a small set of vertices whose removal minimizes the expected spread from a fixed source set. It supports decisions about where to intervene in large interaction networks to control harmful propagation, such as the spread of rumors and infectious diseases. Under the Independent Cascade (IC) model, selecting blockers requires comparing a large number of candidate sets, and estimating their effects on propagation can be costly. We propose SIG (Source-Integrated Greedy), a sampling framework for efficiently finding high-quality approximate solutions. Our key idea is to group the possible sets of neighbors directly activated by the sources according to their effects on blocker selection. SIG represents these groups in a compact weighted tree and computes their probabilities directly, allowing each sample to account for all source outcomes without enumerating them. We prove that SIG produces unbiased estimates of the lower-bound objective without increasing variance for fixed blocking plans, and establish a high-probability quality guarantee through independent validation. Extensive experiments on real-world networks show that SIG has the lowest mean total running time in all main comparisons, with speedups of up to 583x over the fastest baseline. SIG produces solutions competitive with those of prior methods and achieves the highest influence reduction in multiple settings, including on many of the largest networks, where several baselines exceed the runtime limit. Additional experiments show that SIG maintains consistently low running times as graph size and the blocking budget increase, while delivering stronger blocking solutions at larger budgets.
item.dc:creator: Jingbang Chen, Junyao Wang

item.title: Plurality Consensus for $h$-Majority via First-Repetition Rules
item.description: arXiv:2611.16037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the h-Majority dynamics, each of n agents holds one of k opinions and, in every synchronous round, observes the opinions of h agents chosen independently and uniformly at random and adopts a most frequent one among them, breaking ties uniformly at random. Let M_0 be the initial number of agents holding the most frequent opinion, and Delta_0 its bias, its lead over the second most frequent opinion. We show that, for every sample size h >= 3, if Delta_0 >= L sqrt(M_0 log n) max{1, n/(h^2 M_0)} for a sufficiently large constant L, then h-Majority reaches consensus on the initially most frequent opinion within O((1 + n/(h^2 M_0)) log n) rounds with high probability. This is the time bound proved for the DejaVu dynamics with h samples (arXiv:2604.03648); our bias condition is that of DejaVu when h >= sqrt(n/M_0), and larger by a factor sqrt(n/(h^2 M_0)) otherwise. Our main contribution, the analysis of one round, rests on a comparison principle: among all rules that read the same observations and treat opinions symmetrically, plurality maximizes the difference between the probability of outputting the most frequent opinion and that of outputting any fixed competitor. We apply it to the rule that adopts the first opinion repeated among h-1 observations, and otherwise the h-th observation: its output law is the law of the new opinion of a random agent after one round of DejaVu with h-1 samples. Hence, in expectation, one round of h-Majority widens the gap between the most frequent opinion and each competitor at least as much as that round of DejaVu, whose analysis we use as a black box. Independently and concurrently, d'Amore, Rybicki, Shimizu, Shiraga and Vacus (arXiv:2610.40562) obtained, among other results, the same time bound under the weaker bias condition of DejaVu, with a different analysis of one round and a martingale analysis over many rounds.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o D'Archivio, George Giakkoupis, Fr\'ed\'eric Giroire, Emanuele Natale

item.title: Explicit Edit Codes via Multicoloring
item.description: arXiv:2611.16835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any fixed integers $q\ge2$ and $t\ge1$, we construct explicit $q$-ary codes of length $n$ that correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most $2t\log_q n+O_{q,t}(\log\log n)$ $q$-ary symbols. This matches the leading redundancy term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. Building on the standard graph-coloring approach, we use a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to assign multiple colors to each $q$-ary word of length $m<n$. Appending a short, edit-protected representation of an assigned color to the length-$m$ word yields a length-$n$ codeword. The choice among the assigned colors carries additional message information, thereby reducing the redundancy. The construction admits deterministic encoding and decoding in $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{6t+2})$ and $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{7t+2})$ time, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Huiling Xie, Zitan Chen

item.title: Locality Meets Interference: Structure and Scheduling in Radio Multicasting
item.description: arXiv:2611.16844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study multipoint-to-multipoint multicasting in synchronous radio networks with unknown participant locations and unrestricted message aggregation. Let $n$ be the network size, $k$ the number of participants, and $d$ their hop diameter. A supplied distance-two coloring with $C$ colors yields completion within $(C-1)d+1$ slots and at most $nk$ transmissions. In unit disk graphs, coordinates, one-hop neighbor data, and a common degree bound $\Delta_0$ suffice for a $15(\Delta_0+1)$-color schedule. A known fixed separation bound permits optimal deterministic $\Theta(d)$ completion from coordinates alone. Without geometric data, strong selectivity gives $O(d\min\{n,(\Delta_0+1)^2\log n\})$ slots when $n$ is known. Independent random transmission gives $O((\Delta_0+1)(d+\log(k/\eta)))$ slots with failure probability at most $\eta$; for fixed $\Delta_0$, this simplifies to $O(d+\log(1/\eta))$. A star construction shows that the logarithmic term is necessary for this random rule when the degree grows. We extend color schedules to fixed deletions and subgraphs connected over bounded windows of cycles. Separate conditional reductions preserve additive costs under diameter guessing and control parameter-table and cluster preprocessing. Finally, a counterexample shows that pruning and reranking a breadth-first tree can destroy interference-free delivery. For one-hop designated delivery with receiver degree at most $b$, we prove that the optimal schedule length equals the chromatic number of an associated conflict graph and is at most $2b-1$, with matching examples.
item.dc:creator: Qin Xin

item.title: Tight Bounds for Downward-Closed Prophet and Secretary Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.16880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online selection problems subject to arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints, under different arrival orders, with different distributional assumptions. We establish the following bounds: (1) $\Theta(\log^2 n / \log \log n)$ for the standard (adversarial-order) prophet problem, (2) $\Omega(\log n)$ for the (Bayesian, random-order) prophet secretary problem, and by extension, for the standard (prior-free, random-order) secretary problem, and (3) $O(\log n / \log \log n)$ for the free-order prophet problem. Together with complementary bounds established in prior work, these results pin down the asymptotically tight competitive ratios for all these variants of prophet and secretary problems subject to downward-closed constraints. Our results refine and reinforce the big-decisions-first principle by Rubinstein and Singla [2026], establishing a superconstant separation between the random-order and free-order models.
item.dc:creator: Hanrui Zhang

item.title: Near-Optimal Regret for Oracle-Efficient Adversarial Contextual Bandits
item.description: arXiv:2611.17109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study contextual bandits with $K$ actions, a class of $N$ policies, and i.i.d.\ contexts from a distribution that the learner can sample. For any sequence of loss functions fixed before play, we give an oracle-efficient algorithm with expected regret $O(\sqrt{KT\log(2N)}\,\log(2KT))$ against the best policy in hindsight on the realized contexts. This improves the $T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon in prior oracle-efficient bounds and achieves the optimal regret rate in this setting up to logarithmic factors. Our algorithm perturbs policy scores using a Poisson sample of auxiliary contexts. At each sampled context, the perturbation assigned to an action is a Laplace noise draw multiplied by a scale specific to that context and action. We show that choosing these scales to minimize a convex objective determined by past observations yields the stated regret bound. We further approximate the minimizing scales by projected stochastic gradient descent using only an exact offline cost-sensitive optimization oracle that returns the optimum value. Since the table of scales can be large, the algorithm represents the SGD iterates implicitly by storing the random draws that determine each update and evaluates the scales only at queried contexts. Both the oracle complexity and the remaining resource bounds are polynomial in $T$, $K$, and $\log(2N)$.
item.dc:creator: Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi

item.title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.17228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] and Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] with exponential dependence on $k$. Prior works exhaustively search over a $k$-dimensional subspace spanned by the regressors, using conditional moments of the response to test candidates. In contrast, our algorithm is driven by an improved understanding of the moments of the covariates. We show that, restricting to observations with large response values, the degree-$(\log n)$ Hermite moment of the covariates approximately decomposes as a sum of tensor powers of the regressors. The first step of our algorithm can be viewed as a tensor decomposition algorithm for these implicitly represented high-order tensors, which outputs unit vectors parallel to the regressors. A secondary step based on a simple variant of ordinary least squares extracts estimates for the regressors given these unit vectors. We believe our analytic insight and algorithmic components may have applications to designing efficient algorithms for other latent-variable problems.
item.dc:creator: Felix Zhou

item.title: Exact Distances for Parameterized String Matching with Mismatches
item.description: arXiv:2412.00222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two strings are considered to have parameterized matching when there exists a bijection of the parameterized alphabet onto itself such that it transforms one string to another. Parameterized matching has application in software duplication detection, image processing, and computational biology. We consider the problem for which a pattern $p$, a text $t$ and a mismatch tolerance limit $k$ are given and the goal is to find all positions in text $t$ for which pattern $p$ parameterized matches with $|p|$-length substrings of $t$ with at most $k$ mismatches. The number of mismatches is the Hamming distance under the best bijection, which we call the parameterized distance. Our main result is an algorithm that computes the parameterized distance at every position of the text, and hence solves this problem for every $k$ at once. Its running time is $O((\sigma_p^2+\sigma_s)\, n\log m + n\,T_M)$, where $n = |t|$, $m=|p|$, $\sigma_p$ and $\sigma_s$ are the numbers of parameterized and static characters, and $T_M$ is the time to compute one maximum weight matching in a bipartite graph with $2\sigma_p$ vertices. With the algorithm of Gabow and Tarjan, $T_M=O(\sigma_p^{2.5}\log(\sigma_p m))$. Since this bound does not depend on $k$, our algorithm improves the algorithm by Hazay, Lewenstein and Sokol for $k=\tilde{\Omega}(\sigma_p^{5/3}+\sigma_s^{2/3})$.
item.dc:creator: Apurba Saha, Iftekhar Hakim Kaowsar, Mahdi Hasnat Siyam, M. Sohel Rahman

item.title: Geometric Interpretation of 3-SAT and Phase Transition
item.description: arXiv:2509.19740v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interpretation of 3-SAT as a volume filling problem, and its use to explore the SAT/UNSAT phase transition.
item.dc:creator: Frederic Gillet

item.title: Learning-augmented smooth integer programs with PAC-learnable oracles
item.description: arXiv:2602.02505v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an end-to-end learning-augmented framework for smooth integer programs, a broad class of Boolean polynomial optimization problems including MAX-CUT and MAX-k-SAT. An oracle learned from sampled instances predicts a full Boolean assignment for each unseen instance. For fixed-degree objectives, our polynomial-time pipeline, LEAP, linearizes the objective around the predicted assignment, solves an error-budgeted linear program, and rounds the fractional solution. We establish two guarantees. First, for any prediction, the approximation loss of LEAP degrades gracefully with prediction error: it is controlled by an error footprint that quantifies how much mispredicted coordinates can perturb the objective's local coefficients. Second, we bound the pseudo-dimension of the LEAP-induced cost class, yielding a PAC-style guarantee for learning an oracle from a predictor class via empirical risk minimization on instances from an unknown distribution. Together, these results give an end-to-end bound that separates the expected footprint loss of the best oracle in the class from the statistical error of learning. In experiments on MAX-CUT and MAX-SAT, LEAP substantially repairs imperfect predictions, empirical risk minimization selects effective oracle candidates, and the pipeline scales to application benchmarks with up to two million clauses.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Yuan He, Jiang-Tian Xue, Ming Li, Zhi-Hua Zhou

item.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
item.description: arXiv:2603.10655v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well-documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here we analyze intermittent L\'evy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the L\'evy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ($\mu = 2$) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area $\Delta$ in a domain of volume $n$, the optimal expected detection time scales as $n/\Delta$, and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other L\'evy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Stromieri, Emanuele Natale, Amos Korman

item.title: Approximation Algorithms for Scheduling Unrelated Crowd Workers with Contact Delays in Mobile Social Networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.26129v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies a distributed task scheduling problem in which a requester assigns independent tasks to heterogeneous mobile devices (crowd workers) that it reaches only through opportunistic contacts in a mobile social network. The problem generalizes scheduling on unrelated parallel machines: the service time of a task depends on the crowd worker that performs it, every task incurs a worker-dependent contact delay, and the objective is to minimize the total weighted completion time. For identical crowd workers, we tighten the approximation ratio of the Largest-Ratio-First (LRF) algorithm and update the competitive ratio of its online version. For unrelated crowd workers, we show that the time-indexed rounding framework of Im and Li remains valid when worker-dependent contact delays are added, which yields a randomized algorithm with an expected approximation ratio of 1.45; this improves upon the expected ratio of $1.5+\epsilon$ obtained in our previous work for identical crowd workers. We also derandomize this algorithm. To improve computational efficiency, we further propose an algorithm that exploits the optimality of the Smith-ratio order on a single crowd worker, and we prove that it is a deterministic 1.5-approximation algorithm and that its polynomial-time version achieves an approximation ratio arbitrarily close to 1.5. Experiments on synthetic instances and on instances derived from real contact traces show that this algorithm outperforms three variants of LRF in all tested settings, with the largest advantage when the crowd workers are highly heterogeneous, performs on par with a local-search heuristic for unrelated machines, and is within 0.4\% of the optimum on average on small instances that can be solved exactly.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Yeh Chen

item.title: Approximation Algorithms for Matroid-Intersection Coloring with Applications to Rota's Basis Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.03735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study algorithmic matroid intersection coloring. Given $k$ matroids on a common ground set $U$ of $n$ elements, the goal is to partition $U$ into the fewest number of color classes, where each color class is independent in all matroids. It is known that $2\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice to color the intersection of two matroids, $(2k-1)\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice for general $k$, where $\chi_{\max}$ is the maximum chromatic number of the individual matroids. However, these results are non-constructive, leveraging techniques such as topological Hall's theorem and Sperner's Lemma. We provide the first polynomial-time algorithms to color two or more general matroids where the approximation ratio depends only on $k$ and, in particular, is independent of $n$. For two matroids, we constructively match the $2\chi_{\max}$ existential bound, yielding a 2-approximation for the Matroid Intersection Coloring problem. For $k$ matroids we achieve a $(k^2-k)\chi_{\max}$ coloring, which is the first $O(1)$-approximation for constant $k$. Our approach introduces a novel matroidal structure we call a \emph{flexible decomposition}. We use this to formally reduce general matroid intersection coloring to graph coloring while avoiding the limitations of partition reduction techniques, and without relying on non-constructive topological machinery. Furthermore, we give a \emph{fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme} (FPRAS) for coloring the intersection of two matroids when $\chi_{\max}$ is large. This yields the first polynomial-time constructive algorithm for an asymptotic variant of Rota's Basis Conjecture. This constructivizes Montgomery and Sauermann's recent asymptotic breakthrough and generalizes it to arbitrary matroids.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Chaitanya Swamy, Michael Zlatin

item.title: Classes Testable with $O(1/\epsilon)$ Queries for $\epsilon$ Below an $n$-Independent Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2604.05615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study classes of Boolean functions that are testable with $O(\psi+1/\epsilon)$ queries, where $\psi$ depends on the parameters of the class (e.g., the number of terms, the number of relevant variables, etc.), is independent of (or sublinear in) $1/\epsilon$, and is independent of the total number of variables $n$. In particular, when $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small so that $\epsilon=O(1/\psi)$, the query complexity is $O(1/\epsilon)$, matching the known tight lower bound $\Omega(1/\epsilon)$. In particular, if the structural parameters of the class are fixed and $\epsilon=1/\omega_n(1)$ (e.g., $1/\log n$), then the asymptotic query complexity is $O(1/\epsilon)$. This result was previously known for classes of terms of size at most $k$ and exclusive OR functions of at most $k$ variables. In this paper, we extend this list to include the classes: $k$-junta, functions with Fourier degree at most $d$, $s$-sparse polynomials of degree at most $d$, and $s$-sparse polynomials. Additionally, we show that for any class $C$ of Boolean functions that depend on at most $k$ variables, if $C$ is properly exactly learnable, then it is testable with $O(1/\epsilon)$ queries for $\epsilon<1/\psi$, where $\psi$ depends on $k$ and independent of the total number of variables $n$.
item.dc:creator: Nader H. Bshouty, George Haddad

item.title: Lower Bounds for Testing Directed Acyclicity in the Unidirectional Bounded-Degree Model
item.description: arXiv:2604.13577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study property testing of directed acyclicity in the unidirectional bounded-degree oracle model, where a query to a vertex reveals its outgoing neighbors. We prove that there exist absolute constants $d_0\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that for every constant $d\ge d_0$, any one-sided $\varepsilon$-tester for acyclicity on $n$-vertex digraphs of maximum outdegree at most $d$ requires $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^{2/3})$ queries. This improves the previous $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^{5/9})$ lower bound for one-sided testing of acyclicity in the same model. We also prove that, under the same degree assumption, any two-sided $\varepsilon$-tester requires $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ queries, improving the previous $\Omega(n^{1/3})$ lower bound. We further prove an $\Omega(n)$ lower bound for tolerant testing for some absolute constant outdegree bound $d$ by reduction from bounded-degree $3$-colorability.
item.dc:creator: Yuichi Yoshida

item.title: Computational Complexity of the Interval Ordering Problem
item.description: arXiv:2604.24237v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an interval ordering problem introduced by D\"urr et al. [Discrete Appl. Math. 2012] which is motivated by applications in bioinformatics. The task is to order a given set of n intervals with the goal of minimizing a certain objective which is defined via a given cost function $f$ which assigns a cost to the exposed part of each interval (that is, the pieces not covered by previous intervals). We develop a dynamic programming approach which solves the problem with $O(2^n\text{poly}(n))$ oracle calls to $f$ and arithmetic operations. Moreover, our approach yields polynomial-time algorithms for all cost functions $f$ such that $f-f(0)$ is subadditive or superadditive. This answers an open question for the function $f(x)=2^x$. We contrast these results by proving a running time lower bound of $2^{n-1}$ for any algorithm that solves the problem for every function $f$ (with oracle access only) and further proving NP-hardness for some classes of simple functions. Thus, we significantly narrow the gap regarding the computational complexity of the problem.
item.dc:creator: Simeon Pawlowski, Vincent Froese

item.title: Scheduling with Mandatory Breaks: NP-Hardness and an Additive-One Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2609.34254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In classical fixed-interval scheduling, each job of a given set must be processed during a prescribed time interval. The goal is to assign each job to exactly one machine such that no two jobs assigned to the same machine overlap in their interiors, and the number of machines used is minimized. Without further constraints this is interval graph coloring and is solvable in polynomial time through greedy approaches. We study a variant in which every used machine must remain idle during a contiguous break of prescribed length $x$ somewhere in the scheduling horizon. We show that this additional constraint makes the problem hard, except when $x\le1$. First, for every fixed $x\ge2$, deciding whether $k$ machines suffice for the assignment of a given set of jobs is NP-complete, even when all coordinates are bounded linearly in the number of jobs, so machine minimization is strongly NP-hard. Second, for $x=1$, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that solves the problem exactly. Finally, we give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, on every feasible instance, outputs a schedule using at most $\mathrm{OPT}+1$ machines, where $\mathrm{OPT}$ is the true minimum. Unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $\mathrm{OPT}$ machines for any fixed $x\ge2$, so the additive guarantee of one is best possible.
item.dc:creator: Shreyas Ghildiyal, Muralidhara V N

item.title: A Faster Strongly Polynomial Time Algorithm for Submodular Function Minimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.25403v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a strongly polynomial time algorithm for submodular function minimization with overall running time $\widetilde{O}(n^{2}\mathsf{EO}+n^{3})$, where $\mathsf{EO}$ is the running time of a single evaluation of the function. Our algorithm improves upon the previously fastest strongly polynomial algorithms of Lee, Sidford, and Wong (FOCS 2015), Dadush, V\'egh, and Zambelli (SODA 2018), and Jiang, Lee, Song, and Zhang (SODA 2024) that run in time $\widetilde{O}(n^{3}\mathsf{EO}+n^{4})$. Similarly to prior works, our work combines a cutting plane algorithm with the combinatorial arc-finding framework of Iwata, Fleischer, and Fujishige (JACM 2001). We achieve our faster running time by developing an algorithm that runs the cutting plane method end to end, without restarting after discovering arcs and contracting strongly connected components.
item.dc:creator: Alina Ene, Huy L. Nguyen

item.title: Near-Optimal Consistency-Robustness Bounds for Non-Clairvoyant Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2610.29037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of characterizing the optimal consistency--robustness tradeoff for single-machine non-clairvoyant scheduling with predicted processing times. For a fixed number of jobs $n$, Wei and Zhang (2020) established a lower bound on the achievable consistency--robustness tradeoff which is known to be tight only in a few restrictive cases, leaving the optimal tradeoff for general $n$ unresolved. A different worst-case-$n$ regime was introduced by Benomar et al. (2025), who applied the former work's construction to show that for $\lambda \in (0, 1)$, any $(1+\lambda)$-consistent algorithm must be $1 + \Omega(\sqrt{1/\lambda})$-robust. On the other hand, the best known upper bound gives $(1+\lambda)$-consistency and $1+O(1/\lambda)$-robustness, leaving a polynomial gap. In this work, we develop a new lower bound using a multi-stage adversarial construction and a new algorithm that together give a near-optimal characterization of the consistency--robustness tradeoff: for every $n$, our upper bound is within a multiplicative factor $3/2$ of our lower bound, and thus our algorithm is within a multiplicative factor $3/2$ of the online optimal. In particular, our lower bound shows that any $(1+\lambda)$-consistent algorithm must have robustness at least $1/\sqrt{\lambda}$ as $n \to \infty$, while our algorithm achieves robustness at most $\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\frac{5}{4}+1/\lambda}$ for any $n$, matching the lower bound in the leading term as $\lambda \downarrow 0$; our upper bound also closes the polynomial gap in the worst-case-$n$ regime. We additionally show how our algorithm can be made error-tolerant, preserving the near-optimal consistency-robustness tradeoff while incurring only slightly degraded performance under bounded prediction errors.
item.dc:creator: Sizhe Li, Nicolas Christianson, Tongxin Li

item.title: Near-Quadratic Time Multivariate Polynomial Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30907v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\F$ be a finite field. Given $N$ distinct points $\bm{\alpha}_1,\ldots,\bm{\alpha}_N \in \F^m$ and associated values $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N \in \F$, we study the problem of computing an $m$-variate polynomial $f(\vy) \in \F[\vy]$ of individual degree less than $d$, with $d^m \ge N$, that satisfies $f(\bm{\alpha}_i)=\beta_i$ for all $i\in[N]$, whenever such an $f$ exists. This is known as the\textit{ multivariate polynomial interpolation} problem. In this work, given $N=d^m$, we present a deterministic algorithm for multivariate polynomial interpolation over an arbitrary finite field $\F$ that runs in near-quadratic time $N^{2+o(1)}\poly(m,d,\log|\F|)$, assuming $d$ is $\omega(1)$. This bound holds whenever the associated \emph{multivariate Vandermonde} matrix is nonsingular, has constant co-rank, or admits some special structure. In the general case, we give a randomized Las Vegas algorithm attaining the same near-quadratic running time, provided the finite field is sufficiently large and $d$ grows similar to the previous case. Unlike other multivariate interpolation strategies, we do not assume black-box access to the polynomial. In particular, we are not permitted to query arbitrary input points to obtain their evaluations. Our interpolation result follows by combining Wiedemann's classical approach~\cite{w86} for solving sparse linear systems with known bounds for fast \emph{multivariate multipoint evaluation} over finite fields~\cite{umans08, KU11, BGKM23, BGGKU24}. Specifically, our deterministic interpolation strategy relies on a deterministic variant of Wiedemann's approach, which is more commonly used in the randomized setting.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Kanta Mohapatra

item.title: Faster graphic matroid parity: Breaking the $nm$ time complexity barrier
item.description: arXiv:2611.02287v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the graphic matroid parity problem, we are given an undirected multigraph $G=(V,E)$ with $n$ vertices, together with a partition of $E$ into $m$ pairs of distinct edges, and the goal is to find a maximum-cardinality collection of pairs whose union is a forest. This problem generalizes both graph matching and graphic matroid intersection. Graph matching admits the celebrated $O(\sqrt{n}m)$-time algorithm of Micali--Vazirani~[FOCS'80], and graphic matroid intersection admits $o(nm)$-time algorithms due to Gabow--Stallmann~[ICALP'85] and Gabow--Xu~[FOCS'89]. In contrast, for graphic matroid parity, Gabow--Stallmann~[FOCS'84 \& Combinatorica'86] gave an $O(n^2 m)$-time algorithm, and its $\tilde{O}(nm)$-time implementation by Gabow--Stallmann~[ICALP'85] had long remained the best known bound, except in very dense regimes where $m=\omega(n^3)$, in which case the algebraic $\tilde{O}(n^4)$-time algorithm of Cheung--Lau--Leung~[SODA'11 \& TALG'14] is faster. We present a randomized $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2} \sqrt{m} + \sqrt{n} m)$-time algorithm for graphic matroid parity. This is the first algorithm to break the $O(nm)$-time complexity barrier for this problem outside the very dense regime. Moreover, it improves over the previous bounds except in very sparse regimes where $m=\tilde{O}(n)$ and in very dense regimes where $m = \tilde{\Omega}(n^{3.5})$. In particular, when $m=\Theta(n^2)$, our algorithm runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, which nearly matches the $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$-time bounds of Micali--Vazirani for graph matching and of Gabow--Xu for graphic matroid intersection in this regime.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Terao

item.title: Ranking and Unranking Permutations in Heap's Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.05397v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Heap's algorithm is a permutation generation method with very low constant overhead. Its element-interchanging mechanism, however, prevents the standard factorial-base Lehmer code from being applied directly, and to our knowledge no explicit Rank/Unrank algorithm for the Heap order has been published. This paper describes the block structure of Heap's algorithm in terms of rearrangement operators: the net effect of a block-internal traversal is a tail-preserving operator and the block-boundary swap is a top-level swap operator, and together they yield a closed-form recurrence for the block transitions. On this basis a bottom-up Unrank algorithm and a top-down Rank algorithm are built from one and the same closed-form in-block mapping; both run in $O(n^2)$ time and $O(n)$ space and require no factorial-scale precomputed table. The supporting proofs use a synchronized strong induction on the dimension to establish the bijectivity of the trailing-element mapping, closed forms for the final arrangement and for the trailing sequence, the dichotomy of its cycle structure, and the reciprocity of Rank and Unrank. The Heap order is in fact the colex order of the mixed-radix code.
item.dc:creator: Yusheng Hu

item.title: Combinatorial Boolean Matrix Multiplication in $n^3 / 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.06717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For over fifty years, combinatorial algorithms for Boolean matrix multiplication (BMM) and triangle detection saved only polylogarithmic factors over cubic time. At STOC 2024, Abboud, Fischer, Kelley, Lovett, and Meka broke this barrier with a deterministic $O(n^3 / 2^{\Omega((\log n)^{1/7})})$-time algorithm, and asked whether $n^3 / 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ time is achievable. We answer this question in the affirmative, giving deterministic combinatorial algorithms for both BMM and triangle detection running in $O(n^3 / 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})})$ time. Following Abboud et al., we decompose $(A,B)$ into pairs of submatrices $(A_k,B_k)$, called \emph{pieces}, each of which is either sparse or pseudorandom in a sense that forces $A_k\star B_k$ to be nearly all-ones on its vertex sets. Whereas their decomposition produces $2^{O(d^7)}$ pieces at regularity parameter $d$, we obtain $2^{O(d^2)}$ pieces, directly improving the runtime exponent from $(\log n)^{1/7}$ to $\sqrt{\log n}$. Prior work found pseudorandom pieces by repeatedly restricting to denser submatrices, paying worst-case vertex losses at each step that compounded across nested recursion levels, together with an expensive derandomization step. We eliminate the extra powers of $d$ by matching the vertex loss at each step to the size of its density jump so losses telescope across scales, derandomizing witness search via $L_d$-norm estimation so the sampler length stays $2^{O(d)}$, and bounding overlap across the recursion with a fractional density-weighted volume budget rather than raw submatrix volume.
item.dc:creator: Piaoyang Cui, Yiming Liu, David P. Woodruff

item.title: Min-CSPs on Complete Instances III: Nearly Optimal Characterizations of Approximation for Symmetric CSPs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13635v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies complete Min-$k$-CSPs: an instance on $n$ variables has one nontrivial constraint for every $k$-set of variables (so $\binom{n}{k}$ constraints in total), and the goal is to find an assignment that minimizes the number of unsatisfied constraints. They are motivated by the connections to machine learning and data science, as well as the possibility of being testbeds for new algorithmic techniques. Previous recent results presented polynomial-time algorithms for the decision version of every complete Boolean $k$-CSP, which is a necessary condition for any multiplicative approximations for the minimization version, but nontrivial approximation results have been limited to fragile CSPs, 2-SAT, and NAE-3-SAT, leaving the approximability of most complete Boolean Min-CSPs open, including complete Min-$k$-SAT. In this paper, we resolve this question, up to nearly matching factors, for the natural class of symmetric Boolean predicates. Given $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, k\}$, Min-CSP($A$) is a Min-$k$-CSP where each constraint is specified by $k$ literals and is satisfied if the number of true literals belongs to $A$. Let $w(A)$ be the maximum number of consecutive integers in $A$. Our main results for complete Min-CSP($A$) are (1) a QPTAS for $w(A) \leq 2$ and (2) an $\widetilde{O}(n^{w(A)-3})$-approximation for $w(A) \geq 3$, as well as almost matching hardness results for the latter. Our QPTAS for $w(A)=2$ significantly improves the previous $O(1)$-approximation for Min-2-SAT and the $\operatorname{polylog}(n)$-approximation for Min-NAE-3-SAT, as well as extends the PTAS for fragile CSPs (i.e., $w(A) = 1$).
item.dc:creator: Yihwan Chae, Chenglin Fan, Donghyeon Lee, Euiwoong Lee

item.title: Low Rank Matrix Completion via Robust Alternating Minimization in Nearly Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2302.11068v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a matrix $M\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the low rank matrix completion problem asks us to find a rank-$k$ approximation of $M$ as $UV^\top$ for $U\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times k}$ and $V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ by only observing a few entries specified by a set of entries $\Omega\subseteq [m]\times [n]$. In particular, we examine an approach that is widely used in practice -- the alternating minimization framework. Jain, Netrapalli, and Sanghavi [JNS13] showed that if $M$ has incoherent rows and columns, then alternating minimization provably recovers the matrix $M$ by observing a nearly linear in $n$ number of entries. While the sample complexity has been subsequently improved [GLZ17], alternating minimization steps are required to be computed exactly. This hinders the development of more efficient algorithms and fails to depict the practical implementation of alternating minimization, where the updates are usually performed approximately in favor of efficiency. In this paper, we take a major step towards a more efficient and error-robust alternating minimization framework. To this end, we develop an analytical framework for alternating minimization that can tolerate a moderate amount of errors caused by approximate updates. Moreover, our algorithm runs in time $\widetilde O(|\Omega| k)$, which is nearly linear in the time to verify the solution while preserving the sample complexity. This improves upon all prior known alternating minimization approaches which require $\widetilde O(|\Omega| k^2)$ time.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhou Gu, Zhao Song, Junze Yin, Lichen Zhang

item.title: A Unified Algorithmic Framework for Dynamic Assortment Optimization under MNL Choice
item.description: arXiv:2404.03604v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider assortment and inventory planning problems with dynamic stockout-based substitution effects, and without replenishment, in two different settings: (1) Customers can see all available products when they arrive, a typical scenario in physical stores. (2) The seller can choose to offer a subset of available products to each customer, which is more common on online platforms. Both settings are known to be computationally challenging, and the current approximation algorithms for the two settings are quite different. We develop a unified algorithm framework under the MNL choice model for both settings. Our algorithms improve on the state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of approximation guarantee and runtime, and the ability to manage uncertainty in the total number of customers and handle more complex constraints. In the process, we establish various novel properties of dynamic assortment planning (for the MNL choice model) that may be useful more broadly.
item.dc:creator: Shuo Sun, Rajan Udwani, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

item.title: 2-Layer Fan-Planarity in Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2508.17349v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a bipartite graph admits a 2-layer fan-planar drawing. This resolves an open problem posed in several papers since 2015. We also obtain a linear-time algorithm for the one-sided case.
item.dc:creator: Yasuaki Kobayashi, Yuto Okada

item.title: Functional Stochastic Localization
item.description: arXiv:2602.03999v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Eldan's stochastic localization is a probabilistic construction that has proved instrumental to modern breakthroughs in high-dimensional geometry and the design of sampling algorithms. Motivated by sampling under non-Euclidean geometries and the mirror descent algorithm in optimization, we develop a functional generalization of Eldan's process that replaces Gaussian regularization with regularization by any positive integer multiple of a log-Laplace transform. We further give a mixing time bound on the Markov chain induced by our localization process, which holds if our target distribution satisfies a functional Poincar\'e inequality. Finally, we apply our framework to differentially private convex optimization in $\ell_p$ norms for $p \in [1, 2)$, where we improve state-of-the-art query complexities in a zeroth-order model.
item.dc:creator: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian

item.title: An Asymptotically Tight Bound on the Number of Distinct Squares in Circular Words
item.description: arXiv:2609.32084v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A square is a word $xx$ with $x$ nonempty. We study the maximum number of distinct squares occurring in the rotations of a word of length $n$. Amit and Gawrychowski (SPIRE 2017) obtained an upper bound of $3.14n$. Charalampopoulos et al. (CPM 2026) improved the upper bound to $\lceil9n/5\rceil$ and gave a binary construction with at least $3n/2-O(\sqrt n)$ distinct squares for infinitely many $n$. They conjectured an upper bound of $3n/2$. Li and Song subsequently reported an improved upper bound of $5n/3$. We prove that a circular word of length $n$ containing $\sigma$ distinct letters has at most $\lfloor3(n-\sigma)/2\rfloor$ distinct squares. This settles the conjecture and establishes that the leading coefficient $3/2$ is optimal even for binary words. Our proof groups squares by their Lyndon roots and, for primitive words, uses a weighted count of circuits in the Rauzy graphs of the bi-infinite repetition of the word.

item.title: Resolving Tusn\'ady's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06998v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a lower bound of $\Omega_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusn\'ady's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $\Theta_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors. The matching upper and lower bounds are also formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Wolfe's Minimum-Norm-Point Method Generalizes the Simplex Method
item.description: arXiv:2611.12680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wolfe's method computes the point of minimum Euclidean norm in the convex hull of finitely many points. The method is parameterized by an insertion rule and it has been an open problem whether Wolfe's original rule guarantees a polynomial number of iterations (De Loera, Haddock, and Rademacher; STOC'18). We resolve this question by proving an exponential lower bound. In fact, we establish a tight connection to the simplex method for linear programming that allows us to transfer many lower bounds for simplex pivot rules to corresponding insertion rules of Wolfe's method. These include not only Wolfe's linopt rule via Dantzig's pivot rule, but also many other classical, randomized and history-based rules. As a corollary, we obtain the first exponential example for the Lawson-Hanson algorithm for nonnegative least squares, as well as PSPACE-hardness of deciding whether the linopt rule ever uses a given point.
